title: Finite-free model of a bounded-below pseudo-coherent complex near a prime
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\mathfrak p\subset R$ a prime ideal, and $K\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] a pseudo-coherent object [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Assume $K$ is bounded below, meaning $H^i(K)=0$ for every $i<c$ for some $c\in\mathbf Z$. Write $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak p)$ and $d_i=\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}H^i(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\kappa(\mathfrak p))$, where derived tensor is computed by a bounded-above finite-free representative of $K$. Suppose $a\in\mathbf Z$ satisfies $d_i=0$ for all $i<a$. Then all $d_i$ are finite, and there exist $f\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$, $b\ge a$, and a bounded cochain complex $F^\bullet$ of $R_f$-modules such that $F^i=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$, $F^i\cong R_f^{\oplus d_i}$ for $a\le i\le b$, and $F^\bullet\simeq K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R_f$ in $D(R_f)$. Here $R_f=R[1/f]$.

source.place: Tag 0BYP, lemma-lift-bounded-pseudo-coherent-to-perfect; finite-dimensionality and eventual upper vanishing also in Tag 0BCC, lemma-lift-pseudo-coherent-from-residue-field.

proof.text: Choose a bounded-above finite-free representative $P$ of $K$, with $P^j=0$ for $j>u$, using [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Its residue tensor has finite-dimensional terms, so each cohomology space, being a subquotient of one term, is finite-dimensional; it vanishes for $j>u$. Thus all $d_j$ are finite. Choose $c$ as in the hypothesis and put $t=\min(a,c)-1$. Then $H^t(P\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))=0$ and $H^j(P)=0$ for $j\le t$.

source.place: Tag 0BCC, lemma-lift-pseudo-coherent-from-residue-field, finiteness observation; Tag 0BYP, lemma-lift-bounded-pseudo-coherent-to-perfect, first sentence

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-free-complex-residue-degree-cancellation] to $P$ in degree $t$. It gives $s\notin\mathfrak p$ and a finite-free complex $Q$ over $R_s$, homotopy equivalent to $P\otimes_RR_s$, with $Q^t=0$. The support-preservation clause gives $Q^j=0$ for $j>v=\max(u,t)$. Because its degree-$t$ term is zero, $Q$ is the direct sum of the complexes $A=Q^{<t}$ and $B=Q^{>t}$, with the inherited differentials and zero terms elsewhere. In particular $B$ is bounded finite free in degrees $[t+1,v]$.

source.place: Tag 068U, lemma-cut-complex-in-two, direct matrix proof, as used by Tag 0BYP

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], localization preserves the cycle-image exact sequences of $P$, hence $H^j(P\otimes_RR_s)=H^j(P)_s=0$ for $j\le t$. Homotopy equivalence gives the same vanishing for $Q$. For $j<t$, $H^j(A)=H^j(Q)$; in the other degrees $A$ has zero terms. Thus $A$ is acyclic and projection $Q\to B$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Consequently $B$ represents $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R_s$. All scalar extensions here are computed on the bounded-above finite-free representative specified in the item; exact localization also preserves its representing quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0BYP, lemma-lift-bounded-pseudo-coherent-to-perfect, vanishing of the lower summand; Tag 068U, lemma-cut-complex-in-two

proof.text: Tensor the homotopy equivalence $P_s\simeq Q$ with $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$: the equations $uv-1=dh+hd$ remain such equations by tensoring. For $j>t$, the residue cohomology of $Q=A\oplus B$ is that of $B$. For $j\le t$, the terms of $B$ vanish and $d_j=0$ since $t<a$. Therefore $\dim H^j(B\otimes_{R_s}\kappa(\mathfrak p))=d_j$ for every $j$. This avoids tensoring the acyclic lower summand as though arbitrary tensor preserved acyclicity.

source.place: Tag 068U, lemma-cut-complex-in-two, explicit split model; Tag 0BCD, lemma-lift-perfect-from-residue-field, residue ranks

proof.text: Use [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] to regard $R_{\mathfrak p}$ as a local ring with residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. The bounded finite-free complex $B_{\mathfrak p}$ is pseudo-coherent by [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Its residue dimensions are the finite $d_j$ and vanish above $u$. Apply [lem-sc-perfect-local-pseudocoherent-free-model] to its derived object. Obtain a bounded-above representative $M$ over $R_{\mathfrak p}$ with $M^j\cong R_{\mathfrak p}^{d_j}$. Since $d_j=0$ below $a$ and above $u$, replace the zero-rank terms by zero and transport the remaining differentials along these term isomorphisms. Taking $b=\max(a,u)$ makes $M$ a bounded complex of the standard free modules in $[a,b]$.

The bounded finite-free complexes $M$ and $B_{\mathfrak p}$ represent isomorphic derived objects. By [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative], represent that isomorphism and its inverse by chain maps $u:M\to B_{\mathfrak p}$ and $v:B_{\mathfrak p}\to M$. Injectivity of the same morphism bijection says their composites equal the identities in the homotopy category: choose degree-$-1$ maps $h,k$ with $vu-1=dh+hd$ and $uv-1=dk+kd$. With fixed bases, the differentials of $M$, the maps $u,v$ and the homotopies $h,k$ comprise only finitely many matrices because both complexes have finite support.

source.place: Tag 0BCD, lemma-lift-perfect-from-residue-field, omitted spreading details; Tag 0BCC, comparison via derived-lemma-morphisms-from-projective-complex

proof.text: Write each entry of these finitely many matrices as $r/q$ with $q\notin\mathfrak p$, using [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Invert $s$ and the product of these denominators. This produces matrices over a principal localization of $R$ mapping to the chosen matrices over $R_{\mathfrak p}$. The required identities are $d_M^2=0$, $d_Bu=ud_M$, $d_Mv=vd_B$, $vu-1=d_Mh+hd_M$, and $uv-1=d_Bk+kd_B$. They form a finite list of entrywise equations. For each error entry $e=r/q$ that maps to zero at $\mathfrak p$, the fraction equality criterion supplies $w\notin\mathfrak p$ with $wr=0$. Inverting the product of these finitely many $w$ makes all identities hold exactly. The empty products mean $1$. Thus this is a finite fraction calculation, including both chain equations and both homotopies.

source.place: Tag 0BCD, lemma-lift-perfect-from-residue-field, explicit details for the final spreading assertion

proof.text: Let $f$ be the product of $s$, the matrix denominators and the error-annihilators just chosen. Every factor is outside $\mathfrak p$, so $f\notin\mathfrak p$. Over $R_f$, take $F^j=R_f^{d_j}$ for $a\le j\le b$, zero elsewhere, with the descended differential matrices. The preceding equations give a complex and a chain homotopy equivalence $F\simeq B\otimes_{R_s}R_f$. Homotopy equivalences induce cohomology isomorphisms by $vu-1=dh+hd$ on cycles. Exact localization [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] preserves the quasi-isomorphism $Q\to B$ from step 3; the original homotopy equivalence localizes as well. Hence $F\simeq K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R_f$ in $D(R_f)$ with precisely the claimed terms and bounds.

The statement agrees with Stacks 0BYP (more-algebra.tex:20000) and is identical to clones/live and clones/side-live, where the item is still unsplit, so nothing supersedes this delivery. The proof follows Stacks 0BYP, then 068U (lem-weil-pbc-free-complex-residue-degree-cancellation), then 0BCC (lem-sc-perfect-local-pseudocoherent-free-model), and replaces the 'details omitted' of 0BCD with an explicit spreading-out argument. Step checks: the cut degree t=min(a,c)-1 gives both H^t(P⊗κ)=0 and H^{≤t}(P)=0 in either order of a and c. Since Q^t=0, Q splits as a direct sum of complexes A⊕B. A is acyclic because localization is exact (00CS), so Q→B is a quasi-isomorphism. B has residue ranks d_j in every degree, which holds because the homotopy equivalence (not the acyclic tail) is what gets tensored with κ, and B has no terms in degrees ≤t<a. 0BCC applies to B_p, with κ(p)=Frac(R/p)≅R_p/pR_p, and gives a model bounded in [a,max(a,u)]. The K-projective bijection supplies the maps u,v and, by injectivity, the homotopies h,k. In the finite fraction descent, every identity is listed (d²=0, both chain-map equations, both homotopy equations) and each error entry is killed by an annihilator outside p. The assembly correctly uses exactness of localization. Edge cases K=0, u≤t, nonreduced rings and empty products all work. I searched the DAG (rg -L) and found only scheme-level 0BCD nodes, so there is no ring-level duplicate. There are no SGA citations.
